review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally encode the remaining row indices for each elimination column as a finite search domain. A reversible predicate would mark the unique first index attaining the largest absolute active-column value: every earlier value must be strictly smaller and every later value no larger. If nonfinite intermediate row values are reachable, the construction must instead reproduce the required overflow handling and Python comparison behavior explicitly. Run the search once per column and accept a decoded index only after classical verification.
For a finite active column without disallowed intermediate states, exactly one row index satisfies the first-maximum predicate, including the all-zero case before the existing singularity check.

Measure a candidate row index and classically recompute the deterministic first argmax over the current active column. On disagreement or an invalid index, follow a defined retry-and-fallback policy that ultimately uses the classical selection rather than returning an unverified pivot. Preserve the exact-zero singularity check and row swap, then execute the existing elimination, back substitution, finite-result check, residual calculation, named output construction, and exceptions unchanged.
Intermediate nonfinite states and exact Python comparison behavior are not covered by the reported finite checks.

binding.rationale: The formulation now gives strict comparison against earlier values and non-strict comparison against later values, explicitly separating nonfinite intermediate states as requiring a different, unresolved construction. Bind the stated finite-active-column relation only. The generic verification/retry/fallback declaration does not give an executable nonfinite admission/fallback branch, so outside-guard behavior stays unresolved. A conditional pass cannot be treated as whole-domain repair. The assertion that nonfinite states are not covered by reported finite checks is not established by the supplied insufficient-evidence summary; finite test count must not be confused with finite-valued states.

interpretations.meaning: For finite active values, candidate strictly exceeds each earlier value and is at least each later value.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i) and all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices if k > i)
